find: Greater London dominates with 9.7 million people — one in seven of the entire UK.
replace: Greater London dominates with about 9.1 million people — roughly one in seven of the entire UK.
note: F1: Greater London is about 9.1 million (ONS 2024), not 9.7 million.

find: around Birmingham (4 million)
replace: around Birmingham (2.4 million)
note: F2: the West Midlands conurbation holds about 2.4 million, not 4 million.

find: Greater London (9.7m), the West Midlands (4m)
replace: Greater London (9.1m), the West Midlands (2.4m)
note: F1/F2: corrected conurbation figures in the key fact.

find: Today the M6, M42 and M5 motorways converge at Spaghetti Junction;
replace: Today the M6, M5 and M42 all meet close to the city, and the M6 crosses the A38(M) Aston Expressway at Spaghetti Junction;
note: F4: Spaghetti Junction is the M6/A38(M) interchange; the M5 and M42 do not run through it.

find: around 4 million across the wider West Midlands conurbation
replace: around 2.4 million across the wider West Midlands conurbation
note: F2: the conurbation holds about 2.4 million.

find: Around 25% of the UK’s manufacturing output still comes from this region.
replace: Manufacturing still matters more to this region’s economy than to most of the UK.
note: F5: the West Midlands makes roughly a tenth of UK manufacturing output, not a quarter.

find: The inner city is a band of mid-Victorian housing untouched since 1900.
replace: The inner city still holds bands of Victorian terraces, although slum clearance replaced much of it after 1950.
note: F6: inner Birmingham was largely cleared and rebuilt between 1950 and 1975.

find: Edexcel will give you 12 marks across the ‘chosen UK city’ section if you can name and locate features.
replace: Edexcel wants detailed knowledge of one named UK city, so learn it thoroughly.
note: F7: invented mark allocation; there is no 12-mark question on this paper.

find: Sketch the four zones if there is space — examiners reward labelled diagrams.
replace: Sketch the four zones as a quick plan if it helps, then write the answer in prose.
note: F8: fabricated examiner claim.

find: EU enlargement in 2004 added a wave of Polish and Romanian migrants.
replace: EU enlargement in 2004 added a wave of Polish migrants, and Romanians arrived after Romania joined in 2007.
note: F9: Romania joined the EU in 2007, not 2004.

find: Child poverty in Ladywood reached around 47% in 2023, more than double the city average.
replace: Child poverty in Ladywood reached around 47% in 2023, far above the rate in the outer suburbs.
note: F10: Birmingham's own child poverty rate is about 40%, so 47% is not double the city average.

find: For 12-mark evaluations, weigh strategies
replace: For the 8-mark evaluations, weigh strategies
note: F11: 12-mark extended writing belongs to the fieldwork and UK challenges paper, not this one.

find: Always include at least two specific Birmingham statistics — examiners reward precise place knowledge over generic urban theory.
replace: Always include at least two specific Birmingham statistics; precise place detail scores better than generic urban theory.
note: F12: fabricated examiner claim.

find: Studying one city in depth gives you the named places and statistics needed for 8- and 12-mark questions.
replace: Studying one city in depth gives you the named places and statistics needed for the 8-mark extended writing.
note: F13: there is no 12-mark question on this paper.

find: connections to global markets through the world’s busiest container ports at Jawaharlal Nehru Port
replace: connections to global markets through India’s busiest container port, Jawaharlal Nehru Port
note: F14: Jawaharlal Nehru Port is India's busiest container port, not the world's.

find: and the underground Mumbai Metro, with new lines opening through 2024
replace: and the Mumbai Metro, with new lines opening through 2024
note: F15: most of the Mumbai Metro is elevated; only Line 3 runs underground.

find: Avoid generalising about ‘developing countries’ — examiners want Mumbai-specific evidence in every paragraph.
replace: Avoid generalising about ‘developing countries’ — every paragraph needs Mumbai-specific evidence.
note: F16: fabricated examiner claim.

find: In 2022 the UK’s GDP per capita was around $46,000 (US dollars, PPP-adjusted), Bangladesh’s was around $7,300 and Norway’s was around $82,000.
replace: In 2022 the UK’s GDP per capita was around $60,000 (US dollars, PPP-adjusted), Bangladesh’s was around $8,400 and Norway’s was around $130,000.
note: F17: World Bank 2022 PPP values are UK $60,267, Bangladesh $8,449, Norway $129,914.

find: around $59,000, but mid-range HDI of 0.875
replace: around $72,000, but mid-range HDI of 0.875
note: F18: World Bank 2022 PPP for Saudi Arabia is $71,957.

find: The 2024 HDI ranks Switzerland top (0.967) and Niger bottom (0.394).
replace: The 2024 HDI ranks Switzerland top (0.967) and puts Niger near the bottom (0.394).
note: F19: Somalia and South Sudan score below Niger in that report.

find: Saudi GDP per capita ~$59,000
replace: Saudi GDP per capita ~$72,000
note: F18: corrected Saudi PPP figure.

find: The gap between richest and poorest is huge — Norway’s GDP per capita is around 35 times that of Burundi.
replace: The gap between richest and poorest is huge — Norway’s GDP per capita is more than 100 times that of Burundi.
note: F20: World Bank 2022 PPP gives Norway $129,914 against Burundi $1,101, a gap of about 118 times.

find: Norway’s GDP per capita is roughly 35 times that of Burundi.
replace: Norway’s GDP per capita is more than 100 times that of Burundi.
note: F20: corrected in the key fact.

find: the World Bank’s funding of the Mumbai-Ahmedabad rail corridor
replace: the World Bank’s funding of Mumbai’s suburban rail upgrades
note: F21: the Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed line is funded by Japan; the World Bank funded Mumbai's suburban rail.

find: from around £57,000 in inner London to £19,000
replace: from around £57,000 in London to £19,000
note: F22: £57,000 is the figure for the London region; inner London is several times higher.

find: the UN Sustainable Development Goals (17 targets to 2030)
replace: the UN Sustainable Development Goals (17 goals to 2030)
note: F23: the SDGs are 17 goals, split into 169 targets.

find: but contains the world’s second-largest Muslim population
replace: but contains one of the world’s largest Muslim populations
note: F24: Indonesia, Pakistan and India are all close, and the ranking is disputed.

find: Total fertility has fallen from around 4.5 children per woman in 1990
replace: Total fertility has fallen from around 4.0 children per woman in 1990
note: F25: World Bank gives India's 1990 fertility rate as 4.05.

find: For 12-mark evaluations, structure as
replace: For the 8-mark evaluations, structure as
note: F26: there is no 12-mark question on this paper.

find: reduced biodiversity (Amazon deforestation around 10 million hectares a year globally)
replace: reduced biodiversity (global deforestation around 10 million hectares a year, much of it in the Amazon)
note: F27: 10 million hectares is the global figure; Amazon loss is nearer 1-2 million hectares a year.

find: Forestry: Sitka spruce plantations cover around 13% of the UK;
replace: Forestry: woodland covers around 13% of the UK, much of it Sitka spruce plantation;
note: F28: 13% is total UK woodland cover; Sitka spruce is about a quarter of it.

find: Around 70% of the EU’s overall ‘water footprint’ comes from goods imported from beyond its borders.
replace: Around 70% of the UK’s overall ‘water footprint’ comes from goods imported from beyond its borders.
note: F29: about 70% is the UK external water footprint; the EU's is nearer 40%.

find: Renewables and low-carbon together provided over half of UK electricity for the first time.
replace: Renewables and nuclear together provided over half of UK electricity.
note: F30: low-carbon generation passed half of UK electricity several years before 2023.

find: but Hinkley Point C in Somerset is set to add 3.2 GW from 2027 (delayed from 2025)
replace: but Hinkley Point C in Somerset is set to add 3.2 GW, with the first reactor now expected between 2029 and 2031
note: F31: EDF moved the start date to 2029-2031 in January 2024.

find: The government plans to ban new petrol and diesel cars by 2035.
replace: The government plans to ban new petrol and diesel cars from 2030, with some hybrids allowed until 2035.
note: F32: the 2030 date was restored, with hybrids permitted to 2035.

find: The London Pollard Switch Off campaign and Cape Town’s 2018 ‘Day Zero’ crisis
replace: The hosepipe bans across southern England in 2022 and Cape Town’s 2018 ‘Day Zero’ crisis
note: F33: no such campaign exists; replaced with a real UK example.
F1: keeps the correct option in step with the corrected text.

expect: About 9.7 million — roughly one in seven UK residents.
value: About 9.1 million — roughly one in seven UK residents.
note: F1: corrected London figure.
F2: corrected conurbation figure.

expect: Mastering: Names highest and lowest performers (Switzerland 0.967, Niger 0.394), notes the broad north-south split with North America, Western Europe and East Asia at the top, sub-Saharan Africa at the bottom, and identifies anomalies (oil-rich Gulf states). Secure: Three quantitative points with named regions. Developing: Two general points. Emerging: One vague trend.
value: Mastering: Names a top and a near-bottom performer (Switzerland 0.967, Niger 0.394), notes the broad north-south split with North America, Western Europe and East Asia at the top, sub-Saharan Africa at the bottom, and identifies anomalies (oil-rich Gulf states). Secure: Three quantitative points with named regions. Developing: Two general points. Emerging: One vague trend.
note: F19: Niger is not the lowest-ranked country in that report.

expect: Mastering: Sustained argument for and against, considering GDP, HDI, Gini, CPI and food/water security with statistics (UK HDI 0.940, Norway GDP $82,000, etc.). Reaches a justified conclusion that triangulating measures is more reliable but a single composite (HDI) gets close. Secure: Both sides with examples and partial judgement. Developing: One-sided answer. Emerging: List of indicators without argument.
value: Mastering: Sustained argument for and against, considering GDP, HDI, Gini, CPI and food/water security with statistics (UK HDI 0.940, Norway GDP per capita $130,000, etc.). Reaches a justified conclusion that triangulating measures is more reliable but a single composite (HDI) gets close. Secure: Both sides with examples and partial judgement. Developing: One-sided answer. Emerging: List of indicators without argument.
note: F17: corrected Norway PPP figure.

expect: Which agreement set 17 international targets for development by 2030?
value: Which agreement set 17 international goals for development by 2030?
note: F23: the SDGs are 17 goals.

expect: Mastering: Names quantitative changes — fertility from ~4.5 (1990) to ~2.0 (2023), life expectancy from 58 to 70, narrower base of population pyramid, growing middle class (~430 million). Secure: Three changes with one statistic. Developing: General trend without numbers. Emerging: One change only.
value: Mastering: Names quantitative changes — fertility from ~4.0 (1990) to ~2.0 (2023), life expectancy from 58 to 70, narrower base of population pyramid, growing middle class (~430 million). Secure: Three changes with one statistic. Developing: General trend without numbers. Emerging: One change only.
note: F25: corrected 1990 fertility rate.

expect: What share of UK land is covered by Sitka spruce plantations?
value: What share of UK land is covered by woodland?
note: F28: 13% is woodland cover, not Sitka spruce alone.

expect: Hinkley Point C, set to add about 3.2 GW from 2027.
value: Hinkley Point C, set to add about 3.2 GW from 2029 at the earliest.
note: F31: corrected Hinkley Point C start date.
